thread:
Maya: Quick sync — I put a short proposal together for the intake telemetry + bench-sampling handshake. TL;DR: two-tier checks: fast smoke on ingest (sub-second) + scheduled deep sample (nightly / on-change). I think we can avoid blocking on the deep sample for initial admit but still gate final rollout. Thoughts?

Dmitri: +1 to two-tier. Question: what does 'fast smoke' measure exactly? perf-only or perf+sanity?

Maya: fast smoke = runtime sanity (shapes, kv-cache warmup ok), tiny perf probe (p50 token latency), and basic output sanity (no nan / gross tokenization errors). Should be <1s per model. Deep sample is full bench (latency/cost/quantization checks + a small golden set quality pass).

Sara: We should define thresholds for both. Fast smoke should be permissive — only block for panics. Deep sample should have hard failure modes: big perf regressions or quality drop. Where do we store the thresholds? model metadata or a central policy service?

Aj: Put defaults in central policy but allow model-level overrides in registry metadata. That way infra can evolve without touching every model. Also need a version for thresholds so rollbacks are auditable.

Lina: Operational constraint: deep sample runs real workloads and costs $$$. Proposal: run deep sample on a sampling schedule + on any model manifest change. Sampling schedule could be: nightly low-cost window, and on-merge. For high-priority models (enterprise/dedicated) run immediate deep sample in parallel.

Maya: Agreed. Also propose we tag deep-sample results with a "sample_cohort" label (small, medium, regen) to help A/B later.

Dmitri: About the interface boundary — intake should emit an admit-event with minimal metadata: model_id, binary_hash, declared arch, quantization flag, smoke_result. Then an async job picks it up for deep sample. Are we comfortable with async non-blocking admit?

Sara: Yes as long as we have a clear SLA for deep-sample completion and a rollout-level that depends on sample status. E.g., canary traffic allowed immediately, full rollout only after deep-sample pass or manual sign-off.

Aj: One implementation detail: make smoke probe deterministic and small so we can memoize results by binary_hash. That reduces repeated cost when people re-upload same artifact.

Maya: Good call. Also we should record a short telemetry blob on admit-event: {smoke_pass:true, smoke_p50_ms:123, smoke_errors:0} — small JSON stored in registry.

Lina: For deep sample orchestration: queue jobs with priority = customer_tier + model_size. Low-tier models go to cheaper batch pool with longer latency. High-tier go to preemptible or dedicated pools.

Dmitri: How do we surface failures? Slack alert + registry flag + console UI. We should avoid pager noise for benign deep-sample flakiness. Make an incident only for systemic infra failures.

Maya: Agreed. Suggest: failure categories: (1) hard fail (block rollout), (2) flake (retry job + notify owner only), (3) infra (pager). Tag each deep-sample run with category.

Sara: One more tradeoff: golden set size. Bigger golden set yields better quality signal but higher cost. Recommend stratified small set: 200 golden prompts with weights across languages / modalities, and a rotating holdout of 50 per run to detect overfitting.

Aj: That sounds reasonable. Also capture simple eval metrics (exact-match, BLEU-like, embedding-sim similarity) as numeric telemetry so Optimize can recommend quantization/settings later.

Lina: Ops ask: put a TTL on cached deep-sample artifacts and telemetry (say 90d) and a way to re-trigger historical deep-sample on-demand. Storage costs otherwise climb.

Maya: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with these concrete pieces: admit-event schema, smoke probe spec, deep-sample scheduling policy, threshold defaults, telemetry schema, backlog for registry UI flags. Would like signoff from eng-ml before I post.

Dmitri: +1 from me. Add a note about memoization key scheme (binary_hash + model-config-hash) so we don't miss config-sensitive differences.

Sara: +1. Also include examples for console UI wording for "smoke passed" vs "deep-sample pending" to reduce customer confusion.

Aj: +1 but add a short runbook for owners when deep-sample fails QC (who to ping, how to request manual override).

Lina: +1. I'll add the ops SLA table to the RFC. Also, can we include a cost-estimate line for medium model deep-sample? ops needs that number.

Maya: Will add cost estimates (rough) and schedule a 30m sync after RFC. Thanks all. :party-parrot:
